data: -Great Gameplay, a very immersive and addictive experience that will keep you coming back for more
Great game, great atmosphere, great challenge and great fun
Great game with lots of replayability
The soundtrack is [i]amazing[/i], so make it a 10/10
it is well worth full price 10/10

The grand daddy of space rogue lites. This game will brutalize you and have you sprinting back for more punishment. The soundtrack is nonstop bangers, the gameplay is solid, and the dialogue choices slap. It's like a space battle themed choose your own adventure book and I'll never not love it.

I really have no idea why I enjoy getting blown up by the rebels so much. Maybe it's the fantastic level of detail put into the mechanics of the game, or perhaps it's the amazing soundtracks this game has to offer, or possibly the wide variety of content that allows for nearly infinite replayability- no two runs are ever quite the same. However, I do know this: the feeling you get when the Rebel Flagship explodes into tiny pieces of orange shrapnel is rebel-killingly, game-winningly, ship-explodingly euphoric!

You would not expect it from the 8 bit art or the layout, but this game is full of excitement. I don't play games like this usually, but I like RPGs and Strategy games as well as a bit of roguelike so this scratches those itches.
A sort of a spiritual successor to Strange Adventures in Infinite Space, but more in-depth and compelling. A very solid game.

This is my favourite game. I was introduced to it in 2012 by a youtuber and have been playing occasionally ever since. I probably had hundreds of more hours before I bought it on steam and I have won with every ship on hard multiple times, yet I still lose some games. It is such a well made masterpiece of a game with endless enjoyment

It's still awesome.

UPDATE: Since I wrote this review they have added a free expansion pack to the the game. The ADVANCED EDITION (woo WOO wooooooo)! Large parts of the expansion are written by Chris Avellone of Planescape Torment fame. It adds numerous new encounters, a new race of aliens, new sectors and more. I didn't think you could do much to improve this game but they have done a truly impressive job.

I can't stop playing this game. No matter how many AAA titles come my way I always find myself coming back to this game. Perfect for a 5 minute play before work or a hours upon hours in the middle of the night. Each time you play it's a different little space adventure. If you've ever wanted to be Captain Picard or Admiral Adama this is the game for you. Also the soundtrack is well worth the money.
Well thought out game. Lots of variables to balance. Really alot of fun, though not easy even on easy.

This is one of the best space-ship simulators ever made. It is a simple game, travelling from system to system, upgrading your ship as you go and making hard decisions that are constantly thrown at you. You outfit your ship with different modules and different weapons, both having a large variety, and different crew members too.

Your task for this game is simple, survive up until the end, then blow up the enemy ship saving the day (universe? galaxy?). You are charged with taking a ship with limited capabilites and upgrading it into a killing machine. Before, there were clear cut strategies that were able to work. With the additional new bays for the ship, strategies change. Want to suffocate your enemy, go ahead. Want to sit back and let ion cannons destroy the enemy shields allowing a laser to hit their ship, sure. Want to teleport onto the enemy ship, be my guest. There are so many possiblities with strategies in this game. With all of the different races and ships and bays including the new ones, this game has amazing replay value, as two ships you use will quite be the same. Oh and you can rename the people on your ship to give them funny names.

I love this game. There's so much to do, with nearly endless quests and maps and enemies and crew members and... Then you reach the boss and die. The game has a very short campaign, but with unlimited replay value that's not too much of a bummer. The soundtrack is excellent as well. 8.5/10

A wonderfully deep game with strengths in strategy/mechanics, music, and some light story elements. It's a roguelike space combat game. You can add different systems to your ship for different gameplay elements (e.g. having your crew board the enemy ships, cloaking your ship to avoid damage, controlling drones that attack the enemy or buff your own ship). You can choose to be a helpful good samaritan, or you can be a ruthless conqueror. I can't recommend this game enough.
Simple, but exceptionally entertaining. Highly recommend for a relaxing, though at times quite challenging experience.
Replay value is super high and no run is ever exactly the same. 50 hours played and still yet to beat it, I suck but I'm having fun anyway :') (I refuse to play on Easy mode!)

This game is a masterclass in frustration and reward. It’s a wild ride because a single fire in your engine room can end a 40-minute run. It’s simple to learn, but it takes forever to actually master. Even when I lose, I usually want to jump right back in for another attempt.

[The Breakdown]
Graphics: Potato-friendly
Gameplay: Addictive roguelike mechanics
Story: Non-existent (Player-driven)
Difficulty: Souls-like
Grind: None
Worth the price? Absolutely
Rating: 9/10

It's a really cool game in concept, but I always feel horrible after I play it.

I think it's partly because all of the rng happens at the very end of the game, so you'll feel like you're doing well and then get screwed and lose an hour of progress for no reason. The last boss in particular is extremely random and gimmicky, and makes the end of each run feel terrible. I still play it sometimes because early-midgame is fun, but I always end up rage-uninstalling it and being angry for the rest of the day.

FTL is one of those games that never gets old. I've never mastered it, and that's OK, because it's the perfect game to chill to. Just make sure to save 120 scrap for that Weapon Pre-igniter and remember that hull damage is just another resource.

This game isn't for everyone (it's hard!), but that said, it's hands down one of the most replayable, enjoyable games ever made, and that's not even considering the price. You definitely should buy this and give it a shot if you like a good challenge.

This game has a great atmosphere. Every new game is a new journey that happens when you play, with it's own unique feel. This game uses simple and easy mechanic to create deep and charming experience.
Recommended!

My definitive rogue-like, a superb blend of randonmess that punishes and rewards equally. You truly feel like a desperate starship captain every step of the way. DLC plus mods mean that there is always something to come back to.

Name your crew after your Friends, then watch them die Horribly Time and time again as your incompetance as a Captain becomes apparent. Slowly sinking you into Rage and madness as you spend most of your freetime hunting your own personal White Whale..... And thats on easy mode. 10/10 someday ill manage Hardmode....Someday !

Fun, re-playable, always challenging.

Also, a great game to play when trying to unwind, as you don't need to exercise quick reflexes, etc.

Great game. You'll end up putting a lot of effort to unlock all cruisers, and then there are their types...

Each spaceship is smoothly designed so they're pretty much all balanced, and therefore should be strategized differently from the start since resources are scarce and battles get harder every new sector. You'll probably learn the game fast since mechanics are easy, yet there are so many variables interchanging every battle it makes it a pauseable-real-time strategy gem. Normal difficulty is hard enough itself, haven't even tried the thing on "hard" yet.

Hours of fun guaranteed here since replayability's awesome. Highly recommended.
very good wish theyd make easy easier and update more but other then that best game i own

Perhaps one of the best strategy games I have played. I love the simplicity and options. Your choices matter. A combination of Roguelike and strategy game that will make you play it over an over.

Love it!
A really good game, not so easy and not too complicated also. Old but pure gold game. Does not work in full screen on Macbook (MacOS Monterey with Macbook Pro M1)

On accident I took the medicine needed for an entire planet to survive.

11/10

it happens. As for a real review/message to newcomers in case if people get pissed by my quick and unoriginal comment, here:

The game is fun, but can be RNG based, so a great deal of luck is needed for a beginner to win at first. After you start learning your own tricks and tips, the game will be less RNG reliant and more based on skill since you can use that skill to make the best out of a terrible RNG result or maybe even avoid an RNG tragedy entirely.

Learn to play different ships since they are EXTREMELY varied because one may be more fun or easier for you (Those Lanius ships, horry shit lol they are fun and easy to command).

You can board, shoot, hack, set aflame, and send drones to kill off a ship.

Don't be discouraged by early deaths since there will be a learning curve. It will get increasingly fun until you actually complete it. Also, Advanced edition made the game very fun. I highly recommending it for a first playthrough.

9/10

It's an equally fun and frustrating rouge-like strategic space adventure. The game itself is pretty deep, 8 hours in, I'm still learning. I think I'll keep playing, but in smaller doses. While the game is a RNG crapshoot at times, it is incredibly satisfying winning those hard battles and really rewarding when you unlock new ships. I just completed the quest to unlock the stealth fighter ship and it felt amazing. Still lost in sector 8 like always though. *cry* The game is great until you get there. Even on easy I never have the weapons or upgrades to stand a chance against the flagship.

Addictive and fun to play, FTL is the space roguelike that will have you desperatley struggling time and time again to complete it. Along the way you can unlock different ship layouts, recruit different races with different stats, but different weapons and upgrade different parts of your ship and, well every game will be different is what I'm trying to say! Very enjoyable and not very expensive, definitely worth a look if you are interested.

Great game that seems simple at first but has a lot of hidden complexity (I've still only scratched the surface of what you can do in this game). It's really hard at first, but you get to grips with the basics pretty quickly. For anyone struggling to beat the game, I'd recommend watching 'FTL GUIDE RUN!' by LethalFrag on youtube. After watching it, I managed to beat easy one run and then normal the next. I'd failed on easy mode about 10 times before that.

FTL is a brilliant strategy that lets you taste both feeling of accomplishment and an endless despair. The game is unforgiving and extremely cruel, yet most of the scenarios are reasonably manageable. The more you play and study the game, the more you enjoy its charming atmosphere and unmatched replayability. There are only a few things as rewarding as watching the Rebel Flagship turn to dust while the credits start rolling. Once you learn how to exploit the game mechanics, you are in for a very enjoyable ride.

As a fan of roguelikes, I have quite a few in my steam library. Binding of Issac, Crypt of the Necrodancer, Enter the Gungeon, Rogue Legacy, Don't Starve, Spelunky, and more. However, despite having all those incredibly games, FTL still remains my favorite. It's a masterpiece of a game, with simple yet engaging combat, strategic planning, and grueling difficulty make the victories all the more rewarding, and the losses all the more devastating. The game expects a lot from you as the player, but I promise you that, once you've gotten used to the game, you won't be able to put it down.

I drew spaceships like this as a kid. Having them come to life in such a technically precise way is super cool.

In form and function it is similar to the space exploration element of Mass Effect 2, with crew combat onboard ship as well as system development and rts combat. I would complain about the graphics, except that I never stop to think about them during gameplay.

The game is challanging, but not impossible, and there seems to be quite a few possible strategies for victory. I would give this game an 8/10, and say it is definitely worth the price. I will be picking up any sequels or dlc for sure.

Now I must put the game down and sleep. Damn.

Another game that I played a lot more before I bought it through steam. It's fantastic for both long and short gaming sessions, whether you want to burn a few hours or have a few free minutes to play. FTL makes for a interesting IF often a crusing experience every time. Well worth a buy.

Great game for a great price. My only complaints because of how old it is, it does not have proper cloud support and runs won't transfer over to other systems. A shame, but doesn't really effect the quality of this game.

FTL is one of the quintessential Rogue-like games, where players control and operate a spaceship through a hostile universe, where aliens and pirates will attack, offer help, or ask for help on your journey to the end of a randomly generated universe or die trying. Part of the appeal of the game is that the little events your ship will experience in your journey is not unlike an episode of Star Trek, and for that reason, this game is highly loved, but also for its gameplay, with a specific difficulty curve that values persistency and developing strategies to make it to the end. For these reasons, FTL is an easy recommend.

An excellent little game that offers a unique challenge in this modern age of gaming. Without an autosave or free save feature every action is a risk and at first you will loose a lot... but that is part of its charm as every game is different and every playthrough will offer an entertaining diversion.

The retro graphics add a nostalgic charm and the gameplay will definatly appeal to the old school gamers who remember the days when games were hard to win.

It's a fun game, but easy mode is definitely not easy. Learn to "safely" open your craft to vent out fires or kill your crew trying to fight them.
Has a lot of replay value, likely will take many tries to succeed even on easy. The boss isn't extremely hard but will require constant pausing to react to situations.
The game has a lot of content I haven't played yet and I haven't activated the extra, advanced content either.

Note: Do not trust crazy people, mantis people, or unpowered drones. They're bad news. Do not send your crew to help people. Do not let people onto your ship to help you. No level of paranoid is too much.

Incredibly engaging and beautifully difficult game, nothing is more fun than winning in this game purely off of your strategy. No reflexes, no aim, and a very small hint of luck. Rest is just decision making and strategy.

A highly addicting game! After 28 hours play I've finally "won" on easy, but still have 5 ships to unlock as well as alternative layouts on 2 I have got. A lot more play time waiting for me then.
The graphics are simple, but the game is deep and immersive, with plenty of options and strategic depth. There's a lot to learn from playing (and dying) and lots to explore.

three astronauts set out on a mission to save the federation in their trusty spaceship, the Merry Go
their names were: Luffy, Usopp and Nami
later they were joined by Zorro and Franky
Nami was killed by a hostile boarding party
Franky was held back on a quarantined planet
Usopp suffocated while mending a hull breach
Zorro got lost on a spider-infested space station
Luffy went on alone, as he was approached by a patrolling military vessel
"You have a pirate fugitive on board! Surrender him, or face the consequences!"
"What? But there's no one on board!", said Luffy, "You can even search the ship if you want."
Luffy was taken away by the alien militia, leaving the Merry Go to drift indefinitely in empty space

8/10. would search for treasure planet again

It is a classic example of where good game play doesn't need triple A graphics with FXAA, Tesselation or Ray Tracing. Demands very little of GPU Power/Ability.
I have enjoyed this game so much, that when my save file bugged and I lost everything, I was actually excited because it gave me a reason to play more and unlock everything all over again.

This is a my personal favourite game and most beautiful roguelike I ever seen and I ve seen a lot. Compared to isaac it has limitless possibilities and limitless fun, a lot of gamemodes, scoreboard, a lot of items and ways to finish. Quests, interesting story mixed with great sci-fi, choices and progression, wrapped in the perfectly balanced mix of cute 2d graphics, amazing music and great effects. I instantly loved "Subset games" for making this and since then follow their every game.

I refrained from reviewing the game until I actually was able to beat it...

As you can see, that is 37 hours of playing to beat the game on easy.... it was pain.

10/10 experience. Will be continuing to play.

Holy tap-dancing Christ, what is this? This is FTL, also known as "one of the two good things that ever came out out of a Kickstarter project", and that says a lot. You know what else says a lot? The fucking difficulty.

FTL is a little roguelike space combat / spaceship management game where you get to pick a vessel of choice and manage its weapons, systems and crew as you travel across sectors of the Galaxy during an all-out civil war to deliver a message to Federation command while at the same time making mincemeat of any scum that dare stand in your way including rebels, pirates, slavers, brainwashed aliens, and just generally douchenozzles. You'll also travel through different dangerous environments to spice things up a little.

The graphics are simple and make the game look wlecoming to new players. And in fact it is welcoming to new players, but it's just one of those cases of easy to learn, hard to master games.

It is as addictive as it gets. Incredibly simple, and yes somewhat reliant on RNG but so what? A lot of very good games are. Just one more star, just one more run, just one more. Although the playthroughs are similar, the different ship designs force different tactics that keep things fresh. I haven't tried the mods myself but that is yet another reason to enjoy this for another 600 hrs, I understand several are very good.
kind of like you're in Firefly, except you get cancelled after 3 hours instead of 16 episodes

Do not expect to win. On average you will make it to sector 4 with 6 crewmembers and still get screwed over by weapons missing your target while the enemy lands every attack perfectly. its fun but come on. its easy for fucks sake

FTL made me think I liked rogue-likes. But after playing a couple others and not feeling the same rage, despair and, finally, extreme elation on a win, I guess it's just that FTL awesomeness trancends genres.
Never, while playing a game, have I been more aware of my progress or more proud of winnning as when I first beat it on normal difficulty.

I played the cracked version of this way back before. Played lots of hours. Now that I got money, I bought this. Stuck in my library for a long time, now I'm playing it again. I like the pixel art, UI, ship designs, music, and the feeling of upgrading my ship.

tldr.text: Overwhelmingly Positive (96%): players love the gameplay and combat, which 30% of reviews praise.
Complaints are few and spread across different topics, so no single problem stands out.

New players are far less positive than veterans of the game.
